names: UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision
summary: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision, a 347,500-sq-ft, 12-story eye-care tower (with a 5-story south wing and a garden-topped 3-story north wing) at 490 Illinois Street in Mission Bay, opened November 2020 at a reported construction cost of about $237 million; designed by SmithGroup, with fundraising led by the nonprofit That Man May See.

milestones.text: UC Regents approve a $237,000,000 project budget and design for UCSF's new Center for Vision Neurosciences building at Mission Bay -- referred to in UCSF's own campus numbering as 'Block 33' (a different numbering system from the OCII plan-block numbers used elsewhere in this repo), combining the Department of Ophthalmology and the Francis I. Proctor Foundation in a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and 3-story north wing; construction was expected to begin June 2017 with completion targeted for July 2019
UCSF opens the Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois Street

costs.what: Construction cost, Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision

facts.value: 347,500 across three connected buildings (12-story tower, 5-story south wing, 3-story north wing) plus ~75,000 sq ft of parking for 200+ vehicles
University of California, San Francisco; fundraising led by the nonprofit That Man May See

open_questions: Exact opening day within November 2020 is not given by the source found (a November 27, 2020 article announcing the opening); only the month is confirmed.
